threads.body: [General] This provider inherits order `0`, so a user declarative model customizer can run afterward and add a Zipkin exporter after this check (or be prevented from replacing one). Declarative providers are applied by ascending `order()`, with equal orders nondeterministic. Run this checker last, as the config-properties provider already does, so it validates the final model.

replies.body:
Good catch, fixed in 26c3f880b7 — added order() returning Integer.MAX_VALUE, matching what the config-properties provider already does.

Confirmed the mechanics before changing it: DeclarativeConfiguration loads these via Ordered.loadOrderedList (ascending order()), and DeclarativeConfigurationBuilder.addModelCustomizer composes them in registration order via \mergeCustomizer\, so a provider with \order() > 0\ would indeed have run after this check and could have added a zipkin exporter it never saw.
